Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: We applied proteomics-based NMF subtyping strategies to the IPMNs and PDACs to explore tumor heterogeneities and reveal progression features. This analysis showed three clusters, NMF 1 was entirely composed of PDACs. NMF 2 included some PDACs and some IPMNs, while NMF 3 was almost entirely composed of IPMNs with only one PDAC. Most (75%) IPMNs with an associated PDAC were clustered in NMF 2. Use the feature genes in each of the NMF clusters and pairwise comparison between clusters to interpret the differences between NMF clusters and provide a summary of functional and clinical implications.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Proteomics‐based non‐negative matrix factorization (NMF) subtyping of resected intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPMNs) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs) identified three clusters (Table S4G).  NMF 1 comprises only PDACs, NMF 2 mixes PDACs and IPMNs (capturing ~75% of IPMNs with associated PDAC), and NMF 3 is almost entirely IPMNs.  Pairwise differential protein expression (DE) between clusters is tabulated in Table S4H (NMF 3 vs 1, NMF 2 vs 1, NMF 1 vs 2).  Histologically, tissues were macro-dissected ductal epithelium and cyst fluid from 69 IPNs, 76 normal duct specimens, and 32 cyst fluids.  Mutation/treatment: not specified.  Tissue: surgically resected IPN and PDAC.  Assay: proteomics/glycoproteomics.  Dataset reference: Wang et al., Cancer Cell (2025).

Keywords  
• Exocytosis  
• Extracellular matrix (ECM) organization  
• Complement cascade  
• Oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS)/mitochondrial metabolism  
• Interferon response

Candidate Genes  
RAB27B, COL4A1, PGRMC1, C3, NDUFA4, ARHGAP10, IFIT3

Analysis  
Across all contrasts, NMF 3 (IPMN-like) is marked by upregulated exocytosis and secretory pathways (Pancreatic/Salivary secretion; Regulation of Exocytosis) with concurrent down-regulation of innate immunity (Complement & Coagulation) and broad protein metabolism.  NMF 2 (mixed) shows strong ECM remodeling (Focal adhesion, ECM-receptor interaction) and redox biology (Heme metabolism, hydrogen peroxide catabolism) alongside modest suppression of translational machinery.  NMF 1 (PDAC) uniquely enriches cytokine/interferon signaling (MX1, PML; IFN‐γ Response) and neutrophil degranulation, suggesting an inflammation-driven microenvironment.  The shift from secretion in IPMN (NMF 3) to ECM invasion (NMF 2) to immune activation (NMF 1) aligns with progression from non-invasive cysts to invasive PDAC.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtering the NMF 3 vs NMF 1 GSEA results for “Exocytosis” returns Regulation Of Exocytosis (GO:0017157; RAB27B, RAB3D).  In NMF 2 vs NMF 1, “Extracellular Matrix” terms (Degradation of the ECM; ECM Organization) remain top hits.  “Complement” appears only in NMF 3 as suppressed “Complement and coagulation cascades,” highlighting early immune evasion.  “Interferon” emerges only in NMF 1 (“Interferon Gamma Response”), underscoring late inflammation.

| COL4A1  | Up (NMF 2)| Basement membrane/ECM scaffold       | Focal adhesion; ECM-receptor interact |
| PML     | Up (NMF 1)| Tumor suppressor; IFN-mediated gene  | IFN-γ Response; Cytokine signaling    |

| SERPINA1  | Down (3v1)| Serine protease inhibitor       | Complement & coagulation        |

Comparisons  
- NMF 3’s secretory signature (RAB27B-driven) contrasts with NMF 2’s ECM remodeling (COL4A1-driven) and NMF 1’s inflammatory profile (PML, MX1).  
- Immune suppression (C3, SERPINA1) is lowest in NMF 3 but restored/inflamed in NMF 1.  
- Metabolic rewiring (NDUFA4, OXPHOS subunits) peaks in NMF 3, wanes in NMF 2, and partially reprograms in NMF 1.

Implications  
The sequential shift from secretion to invasion to inflammation mirrors IPMN progression toward PDAC.  Early exocytosis modulation may support cyst growth, whereas ECM remodeling in mixed lesions promotes local invasion.  Late IFN signaling and neutrophil activity in PDAC suggest potential for immunotherapy stratification.  Complement suppression in pre-invasive lesions could serve as an early biomarker.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Experimentally validate RAB27B-mediated exocytosis in IPMN cyst fluid.  
2. Assess ECM-targeting therapeutics in NMF 2-like lesions to block invasion.  
3. Measure complement activity in IPMN tissues to confirm immune evasion.  
4. Profile interferon‐stimulated genes in PDAC for immunotherapy response prediction.  
5. Check presence/absence of mitochondrial OXPHOS reprogramming (e.g., NDUFA4) in each cluster; preliminary DE shows up in NMF 3 (log2FC 1.58, FDR < 1e-10).
